record.tranche_reason: Tests whether susceptibility-guided changes to training data alter induction-circuit development, using training-data reweighting and induction-circuit scores rather than reproducing the original training-time analysis alone.
record.gate_note: The paper reports new induction-circuit results for data-reweighting conditions. It does not measure loss falling with token index or test whether that change coincides with a loss bump; it also does not test few-shot task learning or whether previous-token heads causally compose with induction heads. Cited findings from earlier work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study retrains a 2-layer attention-only 3M model with susceptibility-derived per-token loss reweighting (Repress-0x, Baseline-1x, Induce-2x, Induce-4x; 4 seeds each). It measures induction-head formation with prefix-matching and previous-token scores. Its results bear directly on V5: data properties change whether and when induction heads form. Baseline seeds bear weakly on V4 (formation across training runs). It does not test composition (V1), the phase-change and loss bump (V2), ICL in large models (V3), few-shot mechanisms (V6) or sub-steps (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that reweighting training data along susceptibility PC2 modulates induction-circuit formation: suppression nearly prevents it (the conclusion says 'entirely'), and amplification gives earlier, stronger heads. They frame this as evidence that patterning, i.e. inverting susceptibilities to design data, works.
record.recipe_differences: Uses susceptibility-derived PC2 token weights to alter training data and measures induction-circuit development; it is not a direct replication of the original sources' claim about abrupt formation coinciding with in-context learning and a loss bump.
record.method_sensitivity: Induction-circuit development changes with token weighting: Repress-0x, Baseline-1x, Induce-2x, and Induce-4x. Training-score results aggregate four retraining seeds per weighting.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-pattern induction susceptibilities are about an order of magnitude smaller under Repress-0x and rise sooner under Induce-2x/4x. PC2 explained variance is 0.98% for Repress versus 2.96% for baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Susceptibility-based structural signatures of the induction circuit track data reweighting.

record.problems: Uses one small 3M-parameter, two-layer attention-only model setup and four seeds per induction-weighting condition. The score plots aggregate seeds and provide no stated uncertainty estimates. The study does not directly test causal head composition or the proposed coincidence with an in-context-learning gain and loss bump.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported result directly measures induction-head formation or its predicted behavior. Other experiments on UMAP fins and parenthesis-task algorithms do not bear on the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Causal composition of previous-token and induction heads and the [A][B]…[A]→[B] mechanism; only attention-pattern scores are reported.
Abruptness, coincidence with an ICL gain, and the loss bump are not measured.
Not tested; small model only, no token-index ICL measure.
Other families, sizes, architectures and modalities; only seeds of one 2-layer setup.
Whether in-context learning persists under the data conditions; no ICL score is reported.

missing.what: Test loss over training per weighting. Repress-0x has the highest loss, and models diverge in loss around normal induction-formation time (Induce-4x earlier). Single seed each.
missing.versions: V5 (cost of suppression); loosely V2 timing context

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 limits_scope label is removed: V1 makes no claim of invariance to data. The data dependence belongs to V5, where it is supporting evidence. No uncertainty bands are given; Figure 3 aggregates 16 models. Head-count statements are qualitative ('typically one', 'often three').

versions.untested_parts: Tests induction-circuit development using prefix-matching and previous-token scores, but does not directly test the causal composition of a previous-token head with an induction head.
Does not measure induction formation against loss falling with token index, a sharp in-context-learning gain, or a bump in training loss.
Uses a small 3M-parameter model; does not measure most in-context learning in large transformers.
Reports results across retraining seeds for one two-layer, attention-only model setup; does not test other model families, sizes, architectures, or modalities.
Tests whether induction-circuit formation changes with training-data weighting. Does not test whether in-context learning persists under these data conditions.
Does not study few-shot task learning or compare its mechanisms with induction heads.
Does not test whether induction formation consists of multiple sub-steps or overlapping transitions.
